lifecycleReconciliationV1.axisNote: Four distinct, deliberately unmerged facts per surface: endpointExists (code/route/service is present), reachable (a live probe succeeded; UNPROBED where no live check was run), hasInRepoCaller (a real caller was found by static search), canonicalOwner (this transport is THE selected production path for its capability, not merely present). A surface can be reachable with zero callers, or have a caller while unreachable, or exist canonically without having been live-probed this pass.

surfaces.evidence: Repeated exhaustive search (this pass and the prior caller audit) found zero client construction or fetch to /api/trpc outside an example comment in the mount file itself. A dormant server mount with no confirmed caller is DORMANT, not LEGACY (nothing was ever removed or superseded) and not EXPERIMENTAL (it is a complete, typed router, not a prototype).

Traced retrieval-client.ts's real probe order in checkRetrievalHealth(), not just its comment: step 1 (gRPC) is gated on RETRIEVAL_GRPC_ENABLED, step 2 (this HTTP path) on RETRIEVAL_HTTP_ENABLED. Both default false in env.server.ts (parseBoolean(..., false)) and neither is set in .env or .env.local -- confirmed by direct grep of both files (zero matches) -- so this branch is skipped by current configured code path even though it is live. This repo's own PROTO-02B live snapshot (tasks.md, 2026-09-23) reports this exact service READY_FULL at :8100 -- the healthiest of the three candidate paths, yet not the one the app's default config selects. Classified OPTIONAL (present, healthy, has a real caller function, but config-gated off) rather than COMPATIBILITY, since it is not a fallback FROM the canonical path -- current config never reaches it at all.
surfaces.operatorDecisionNeeded: RETRIEVAL_HTTP_ENABLED/RETRIEVAL_GRPC_ENABLED default to false, so the app's configured retrieval path bypasses this READY_FULL service in favor of a DEGRADED one (see the go-search-service entry below). Not changed here -- a config default change is exactly the kind of decision this reconciliation pass is scoped to surface, not make.

surfaces.evidence: Same probe-order trace as the HTTP entry above; step 1 gated on RETRIEVAL_GRPC_ENABLED, default false, unset in both env files. PROTO-02B (tasks.md) records gRPC :50053 as 'published, unprobed' -- a port being published is explicitly not treated as a gRPC health/method proof per that entry's own caveat, reused here rather than re-asserted.

GO_SEARCH_URL=http://localhost:8096 is the only one of the probe-order env conditions actually set in .env.local. Given RETRIEVAL_GRPC_ENABLED=false and RETRIEVAL_HTTP_ENABLED=false (both default, unset), retrieval-client.ts's real code path (not the leading comment) falls through gRPC and go-retrieval-HTTP to this branch -- this is the live default retrieval path for this transport family today, by configuration, traced through actual conditionals. Reachability is DEGRADED, not healthy: PROTO-02B's live snapshot (tasks.md, 2026-09-23) reports this exact service as DEGRADED at :8096 with qdrantConnected=false.
surfaces.operatorDecisionNeeded: The config-selected canonical retrieval path is degraded (qdrantConnected=false) while a healthier alternative (go-retrieval-service :8100, READY_FULL) sits disabled by default one gate away. This is a real, named architectural tension surfaced by combining this pass's static config trace with PROTO-02B's independent live probe -- not resolved, not switched, not restarted here.

surfaces.evidence: embedding-client.ts gates its gRPC path on ENV.EMBEDDING_GRPC_ENABLED (env.server.ts default false); not set in .env or .env.local (grepped, zero matches). Asymmetric with TurboVec, where the local .env explicitly sets TURBOVEC_SIDECAR_GRPC_ENABLED=true -- this repo enables gRPC selectively per-service, not uniformly, and that per-service enable state is itself real evidence, not noise.

Already documented in callerAudit above: its gRPC placeholder defaults to :50051 while configured retrieval gRPC is :50053, and it is never actually initialized -- its real retrieve path uses HTTP. A wrapper whose named transport is provably never exercised and whose default config is internally inconsistent is LEGACY, not COMPATIBILITY (compatibility implies the alternate path still genuinely works if selected; this one's gRPC path does not).
